'''Jason Keema Hart''' (born April 29, 1978) is an American [[basketball]] coach and former professional player who is currently an assistant coach for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]].

== College career ==
From 1996 to 2000, he attended [[New York (state)|New York]]'s [[Syracuse University]], where he became the first freshman in the [[Big East Conference]]'s history to lead it in minutes played.<ref name="nunes">{{cite news |last1=Sigel |first1=Ben |title=Former Syracuse guard Jason Hart won't join Mike Hopkins' staff at UW |url=https://www.nunesmagician.com/2017/3/25/15058556/former-syracuse-guard-jason-hart-wont-join-mike-hopkins-staff-at-uw |access-date=May 4, 2024 |work=Troy Nunes is an Absolute Magician |publisher=SB Nation |date=March 25, 2017}}</ref> Later on, he earned other accolades as an [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] player, such as becoming his college's all-time leader in steals<ref name="nunes" /> and second place among assist leaders.<ref name="nunes" /> As a senior, Hart made the Big East's All-First Team.<ref name=wolves_tc_roster/> He was also selected to the Syracuse All-Century Basketball team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball All-Century Team |url=https://cuse.com/sports/2009/2/3/sidebar_133 |website=Syracuse.com |publisher=Syracuse.com |access-date=May 4, 2024}}</ref>

== NBA career ==
Hart began his career with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2000–01 NBA season|2000–01 season]], but he only saw action in one game, scoring two points.<ref name="br">{{cite web |title=Jason Hart Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hartja01.html |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=May 4, 2024}}</ref>

Starting the [[2001–02 NBA season|2001–02 season]] in the newly created [[NBDL]] with the [[Asheville Altitude]],<ref name="Orange">{{cite news |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Orange update: Jason Hart not quite ready to give up on NBA |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2010/07/orange_update_jason_hart_not_q.html |access-date=May 1, 2024 |publisher=Syracuse.com |date=July 8, 2010}}</ref> he was called in December by the [[San Antonio Spurs]], appearing in 10 games.<ref name="Orange" /> He played in the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek A1 League]] with [[Makedonikos BC]] in 2002–03, returning to the Spurs for the [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04 season]], where he played in 53 games, averaging 3.3 points.<ref name="br" />

Hart was signed to a three-year, $5 million contract by the Bobcats as a free agent before the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]],<ref name="br" /> and made the first steal in Bobcats history in their first game. Previously, in a 126-125 losing effort in their first preseason game, Hart made a three-point shot as time expired to send the game against the [[Washington Wizards]] into a second overtime period en route to 19 points.

In the 2004–05 season, Hart set career highs in many categories including: points per game (9.5), assists per game (5.0), and rebounds per game (2.7).<ref name="br" /> He finished third in the league in assist-to-turnover ratio, with 3.6 assists for every turnover. After the season, Hart was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Bobcats acquire Voskuhl, trade Hart |access-date=May 4, 2024 |agency=UPI |date=August 2, 2005 |url=https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2005/08/02/Bobcats-acquire-Voskuhl-trade-Hart/63991123031902/}}</ref>

On March 2, 2007, Hart was waived by the Kings.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2785122 Kings waive seldom-used backup guard Hart], March 1, 2007</ref> He was signed a few days later by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/hart-conroy-clippers-030507.shtml Clippers sign Jason Hart, cut Will Conroy], March 5, 2007</ref> On July 13, 2007, Hart signed with the [[Utah Jazz]] on a two-year, $5 million contract.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=2936326 Jazz sign Hart]</ref> Originally serving as the backup to [[Deron Williams]], an injury forced him to sit for 8 games.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Buckley |first1=Tim |title=Jazz's Hart says he has bulging disc in back |url=https://www.deseret.com/2008/2/1/20068045/jazz-s-hart-says-he-has-bulging-disc-in-back/ |access-date=May 4, 2024 |publisher=Deseret News |date=February 1, 2008}}</ref> [[Ronnie Price]]'s solid play during that time nearly removed him from the rotation.

On July 23, 2008, Hart was traded back to the Clippers in exchange for [[Brevin Knight]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3502505 Clippers send Knight to Jazz, get reunited with Hart]</ref>

On February 27, 2009, Hart was waived by the Clippers.<ref>[http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/sports_blog/2009/02/clippers-waive.html Clippers waive Jason Hart]</ref>

On March 3, 2009, Hart was signed by the Nuggets for the remainder of the season.<ref name="br" />

On September 28, 2009, Hart signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref name=wolves_tc_roster>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/training_camp_roster_2009_09_27.html TIMBERWOLVES: Training Camp Roster]</ref> He was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] on December 29, 2009, for [[Alando Tucker]] and cash.<ref name="tucker">{{cite news |title=Suns Trade Tucker to 'wolves for Hart |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/suns-timberwolves-0/ |access-date=May 4, 2024 |agency=Sportsnet |date=December 29, 2009}}</ref> The Suns immediately waived him.<ref name="tucker" /> On February 5, 2010, Hart signed a ten-day contract with the [[New Orleans Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4890638|title=Hornets sign Hart to 10-day as injury insurance|date=February 5, 2010}}</ref> Hart's final NBA game was on February 10, 2010, in a 93–85 win over the Boston Celtics. In his final game, Hart recorded two assists and one rebound.

==Coaching career==
After his playing career ended, Hart coached [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball in Los Angeles and served as head coach at [[William Howard Taft High School (Los Angeles)|Taft High School]] in LA.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=Boys' basketball: Jason Hart looks forward to challenge at Taft |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/blogs/varsity-times-insider/story/2011-07-26/boys-basketball-jason-hart-looks-forward-to-challenge-at-taft |access-date=March 26, 2025 |publisher=Los Angeles Times |date=July 26, 2011}}</ref>  On May 12, 2012, Hart was hired as an assistant coach at [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]], under head coach [[Marty Wilson (basketball)|Marty Wilson]].<ref>{{cite web| title = Pepperdine hires former Syracuse standout, NBA guard Jason Hart as assistant | publisher = NBCSports.com | year = 2012 | url =http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/05/12/pepperdine-hires-former-syracuse-standout-nba-guard-jason-hart/ | access-date = May 12, 2012}}</ref> In 2013, he joined [[Andy Enfield]]'s staff at the [[University of Southern California]].<ref>[http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/varsitytimesinsider/2013/04/boys-basketball-ex-taft-coach-jason-hart-is-headed-to-usc.html Boys' basketball: Ex-Taft Coach Jason Hart is headed to USC]</ref> In 2021, he was named the head coach of the [[NBA G League Ignite]], a developmental team for players coming out of high school that played against other teams in the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/jason-hart-named-head-coach-of-nba-g-league-ignite/n-5732411 |title=Jason Hart Named Head Coach of NBA G League Ignite |website=OurSports Central |date=August 12, 2021}}</ref> In March of 2024, NBA G League President [[Shareef Abdur-Rahim]] announced that the G League Ignite program would be shut down after the season citing "the changing basketball landscape, including the NCAA's Name, Image and Likeness (NIL) policy and the advent of collectives and the transfer portal" as the main factors.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-g-league-ignite-to-conclude-its-final-season |title=NBA G League Ignite to conclude its final season |website=nba.com |date=March 21, 2024}}</ref> With the program ending, Hart was out of a job.  However, on April 22, he was hired as an assistant coach under [[Mark Pope]] at the [[University of Kentucky]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2024/04/22/jason-hart-named-assistant-coach-of-kentucky-mens-basketball/ |title=Jason Hart Named Assistant Coach of Kentucky Men’s Basketball |website=ukathletics.com |date=April 22, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal==
Jason Hart was born in [[Los Angeles, California]]. He is married to his high school sweetheart, Brandi Hart. They have two sons - Jason Jr. and Justin. Hart's cousin is 2011–12 [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball]] player [[Brandon Triche]].<ref>[http://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7757 Syracuse University Athletics - 2011-12 Men's Basketball Roster]</ref>
